history.daily_question: When I see beauty or truth in someone else's form, do I understand what makes it real, or only mimic the shape and miss the life inside?
history.carry_question: Where am I today copying someone else's form instead of discovering what wants to live through me?
history.surrender_question: What false success am I defending as though it were mine to earn, rather than entrusting to God's ordering?
history.daily_action: Today, when I notice envy or the urge to imitate, I will pause and ask: What is alive in me that wants expression? Then I will act from that, however small or unpolished, rather than perform.
history.evening_question: Did I try to be beautiful or right, or did I simply show up as myself and let God work? What did I learn from the difference?

history.daily_question: Where am I still performing frugality or hardship for an audience, and what might honest simplicity look like just for me today?
history.carry_question: When I feel tempted to mention my sobriety, my discipline, or my efforts today, can I notice the urge and let it pass without performing?
history.surrender_question: What outcome or proof of my growth am I still grasping for, and can I entrust my becoming to God's presence instead of my own monitoring?
history.daily_action: Today, I will do one ordinary task—wash a dish, make a call, listen to someone—with full attention and no internal audience, simply because it is before me and it matters.
history.evening_question: Where did I act without needing to see myself act, and where did I slip back into proving something? What can I hand over to God's keeping tonight?

history.daily_question: When I am tempted to grasp for certainty or push ahead of God's timing today, can I instead lift my heart briefly and trust His care?
history.carry_question: Where today might I mistake delay or difficulty for abandonment rather than an invitation to remember God's presence?
history.surrender_question: What outcome or assurance am I trying to manufacture this morning that I can instead entrust to God's timing and care?
history.daily_action: Today, when I face a small obstacle or delay, I will pause and name one virtue available in it—courage, patience, honesty—and choose one small action that exercises it.
history.evening_question: Did I notice God's presence in any ordinary moment today, or did I spend the day braced against what might go wrong?

history.daily_question: Where am I still trying to think my way into clarity instead of letting life show me what I need to know?
history.carry_question: When I'm tempted to explain, convince, or fix someone today, can I pause and notice what I actually see?
history.surrender_question: What outcome am I rehearsing in my mind that I could set down and let God hold while I stay present to what's actually in front of me?
history.daily_action: Today, when someone tells me about a problem or choice, I will resist the urge to offer advice or judgment. I will ask one honest question and listen to the answer without planning my reply.
history.evening_question: Did I trust my own seeing today, or did I let fear whisper interpretations? What might I learn if I let one thing remain uncertain and unresolved?

history.daily_question: Where am I trying to force a result today, and what if weakness or surrender might actually move me closer to what matters?
history.carry_question: When I feel stuck or afraid today, can I notice what I am actually gripping, and ask if loosening it might reveal a next step?
history.surrender_question: What outcome am I holding so tight that it has stopped me from moving? Can I name it to God and stay willing to act anyway, without the guarantee?
history.daily_action: When someone frustrates or disappoints me today, I will pause and ask: What is mine to do here, and what belongs to them or to time? Then I will act once, without force, and let the rest go.
history.evening_question: Where did I force something today and feel the strain, and where did I let go and find I was still moving forward? What can I trust a little more tomorrow?

history.daily_question: Can I tend to God's presence in this ordinary day the way I tend a fire—constantly, without shame, letting it warm everything I touch?
history.carry_question: Where today might I quit God's presence to chase something easier—and what would it cost to stay?
history.surrender_question: What outcome am I gripping so hard that I cannot feel God's presence, and can I name it to Him without trying to fix it first?
history.daily_action: In one conversation today—at work, at home, with someone I'm struggling with—I will speak or listen as if God is present in the room. I will not perform piety. I will attend.
history.evening_question: Did I slip into trifles today, or did I catch myself and return to what actually matters? What am I still holding too tight?

history.daily_question: When my child fails, my cup breaks, my plans scatter—can I meet it with the same steady gaze I turn on others' sorrow, or do I still believe my life should be exempt?
history.carry_question: What small loss or change have I already accepted today in someone else's life—and am I still resisting it in my own?
history.surrender_question: Can I release my demand that my sorrow be less than my neighbor's, and trust that God meets both of us in loss, without protecting me from its truth?
history.daily_action: Before one difficult moment today, I will pause, entrust the outcome to God, and take one kind or honest step.
history.evening_question: Where did I fight my heart's desire today, or cling to keeping something I could not keep—and can I lay that struggle down tonight and ask God what I am learning instead?

history.daily_question: What am I still trying to fix or improve in myself or others that might soften if I simply stepped back and allowed things to find their own way?
history.carry_question: When I rush to manage someone else's choices or character today, can I notice it and pause?
history.surrender_question: What outcome am I demanding—about myself, another person, or how this day should unfold—that I can name to God and then simply tend to what is mine to do?
history.daily_action: In one conversation today, I will listen without offering advice or judgment, and afterward I will notice what it felt like to simply receive what the other person said.
history.evening_question: Where did I try too hard to control something today, and where did I find I could trust the moment more than my worry allowed?

history.daily_question: What if the thing I cannot answer is exactly where wisdom begins, not where I have failed?
history.carry_question: When I feel the urge to explain or defend myself today, can I pause and ask what I am really protecting?
history.surrender_question: What outcome am I gripping today—approval, understanding, being right—that I can release to God while still showing up and doing my part?
history.daily_action: In one conversation today, I will listen more than I speak and notice what I learn by not rushing to answer or advise.
history.evening_question: Where did I pretend to know when I could have admitted confusion, and where did I act with an honest heart instead?

history.daily_question: What strength in me today comes from holding lightly, and what am I still trying to grip as if my life depends on forcing it?
history.carry_question: When I reach for approval or certainty today, can I notice it and set it down like the infant does—without shame, without forcing?
history.surrender_question: What outcome am I still trying to guarantee or defend today, and what if I brought my honest effort and then let God—or the unfolding itself—carry what I cannot?
history.daily_action: Today, I will speak one honest thing I usually hide, or listen to one person without planning my reply, staying present to their actual voice rather than my version of them.
history.evening_question: Where did I tighten or perform today, and where did I manage to stay a little simpler, truer, or kinder than my fear wanted me to be?

history.daily_question: When something I want passes by or hasn't arrived yet, can I notice the difference between wise waiting and the small, tight fist of desire?
history.carry_question: Today, when I'm offered something or waiting for something, can I feel the difference between desire and dread?
history.surrender_question: What outcome or opinion about myself am I gripping, and can I leave it with God while still showing up honestly in my responsibilities?
history.daily_action: When I face a choice about taking or refusing something today—food, help, praise, rest—I will pause and ask whether I am choosing with my own judgment or reacting from fear of judgment or obligation.
history.evening_question: Where did I act from my own clear judgment today, and where did I grip tighter because I was afraid? What can I give to God about that?

history.daily_question: What ordinary work lies before me today—and am I willing to set about it heartily, trusting that God moves through my small, faithful efforts?
history.carry_question: When I feel the urge to control or hurry today, can I pause and ask: What work is actually mine, and what am I trying to do that belongs to God?
history.surrender_question: What outcome am I holding too tightly—and can I offer it to God today while staying present and responsible for the next right action?
history.daily_action: Today, I will choose one small task—a conversation, a kindness, a step in my recovery—and do it with full attention, as prayer, trusting that my faithfulness is enough.
history.evening_question: Where did I catch myself trying to earn or prove something today, and where did I instead simply show up and do the work? What can I leave with God tonight?

history.daily_question: When I meet someone whose views anger or unsettle me, can I stay curious about what I don't yet see instead of defending my rightness?
history.carry_question: What belief about myself or another person am I defending today instead of questioning?
history.surrender_question: Can I release my certainty that I understand someone else's motives, and trust God to show me what I'm missing?
history.daily_action: Today, when I disagree with someone, I will listen for one true thing they are saying before I explain why they are wrong.
history.evening_question: Did I defend my view, or did I stay open long enough to learn something? What one thing surprised me about someone today?

history.daily_question: If God is always near and I am prone to leave Him alone, what small act of remembrance can I choose in the next hour, without performance or strain?
history.carry_question: When I rush through a task without naming God's presence, what am I refusing to see or know?
history.surrender_question: What outcome—approval, control, safety, certainty—am I demanding today that I can practice releasing into God's hands while still showing up and acting with care?
history.daily_action: In one ordinary moment today—eating, walking, listening to someone—I will pause and remember that I am not alone, naming God's presence silently and continuing the task without performance, as Brother Lawrence did in the kitchen.
history.evening_question: Where did I remember God today, and where did I forget? What small remembrance felt easiest, and what kept me distant, and can I bring both to God now without judgment?

history.daily_question: Am I willing today to notice what moves through me without needing to name or control it—and to trust that dependence itself is the doorway?
history.carry_question: When I feel the urge to control someone or fix a problem today, can I notice it without shame and ask what I actually can tend?
history.surrender_question: What outcome am I still gripping—and can I return it to God's hands while staying awake and honest about my small, real responsibility?
history.daily_action: Today I will speak one truth that costs me something, to one person, without explaining or justifying it—and notice what happens when I let the word go.
history.evening_question: Where did I act without needing to be right, and where did I cling? What did the difference feel like in my body and heart?

history.daily_question: Where am I forcing clarity or control today when the deepest truth might live in what I cannot see or name?
history.carry_question: When I meet confusion or resistance today, can I notice where I'm gripping for control instead of listening?
history.surrender_question: What outcome am I demanding certainty about that I can lay down today, trusting God even if I never see how it unfolds?
history.daily_action: Today, I will speak one truth simply and without embellishment, then release the result. I will not rehearse or defend it.
history.evening_question: Where did I insist on understanding before acting, and where did I move forward with partial sight? What can I thank God for tonight?

history.daily_question: When I'm tempted to arrange myself for approval today, can I notice the small muscular effort of it before I continue?
history.carry_question: What small arrangement of myself did I make before speaking or acting today—and what shifted when I noticed it?
history.surrender_question: Am I willing today to disappoint one expectation I've been carrying about how I should appear, just to feel what actual ease might be?
history.daily_action: Once today, when I catch myself adjusting my stance, tone, or offering for approval, I'll pause and name it silently—not to shame myself, but to mark the moment and move on.
history.evening_question: Did I notice any moment when I relaxed the arrangement of myself, and what was different about how I moved or spoke?

history.daily_question: When I move through today's ordinary tasks, am I tending my own judgment—or have I already surrendered it to someone else's urgency?
history.carry_question: In this hour, where am I tending something carefully, and where might I actually be gripping?
history.surrender_question: What small decision today have I already made without noticing, and what would it cost to reclaim it?
history.daily_action: Before you say yes to something—a request, a worry, a plan—pause and notice: am I choosing this, or am I already following someone else's track?
history.evening_question: What did I tend today that mattered, and what was I defending that I could have left alone?

history.daily_question: When I judge someone today, can I notice what I already assume is true before I investigate what actually is?
history.carry_question: Before I react to what someone did or said, what am I assuming I already know about them?
history.surrender_question: Can I let go of needing to be right about this person today, just for the next hour?
history.daily_action: In one conversation today, pause and ask one genuine question before you speak your assessment—not to change their mind, but to find out what you don't yet see.
history.evening_question: Did I investigate or assume? What did I learn by asking instead of deciding?

history.daily_question: When I cross paths with someone today—on transit, at work, in line—can I notice them the way Whitman notices the ferry crowd: as curious, particular, and mysteriously worth my actual attention?
history.carry_question: What is actually curious or particular about someone I encounter today that I might miss if I stay in my own thought?
history.surrender_question: What story am I already telling about someone before I actually look at them or listen to what they say?
history.daily_action: During one ordinary interaction today, notice one detail about the other person—a gesture, a word choice, an expression—without narrating it. Just register it.
history.evening_question: When I genuinely noticed someone today without judgment, what changed in how I felt in my own body or thought?

history.echo_title: Song of Myself · section 14 · excerpt, stanza 5
history.daily_question: When I notice myself valued only for how I appear, can I distinguish between genuine care for dignity and the small, tight performance that erases what else I am?
history.carry_question: Today, when someone notices me, can I feel whether I'm performing or simply present?
history.surrender_question: What assumption about being valued or seen am I willing to notice without immediately defending or fixing it?
history.daily_action: Choose one moment today—a conversation, a task, a mirror—and notice the muscular effort of performing versus the ease of simply being; nothing to change, only to see.
history.evening_question: What did I notice about the difference between being valued for my appearance and being met as I actually was today?

history.echo_title: A Song of the Rolling Earth · section 3 · excerpt, stanza 5–6
history.daily_question: When I strike at something today—a decision, a confrontation, a project—how will I know if I've stopped at the right moment rather than pushed past it?
history.carry_question: When I finish something today, can I notice whether I'm pushing past its natural stopping point?
history.surrender_question: What am I still trying to complete or explain that might be wiser left as it is?
history.daily_action: Today, after one deliberate action, I will notice the impulse to follow it with another—and choose to pause and wait, even briefly, before deciding whether the next move belongs.
history.evening_question: What did I finish today, what did I leave unfinished, and did either one feel right—or did I discover the difference only in hindsight?

history.daily_question: When I catch myself performing agreement to smooth things over today, can I notice what truth I'm actually swallowing in that moment?
history.carry_question: Today, when someone asks my view or needs my support, what will I actually say instead of what I think they want?
history.surrender_question: Am I willing to disappoint someone's expectation of me rather than abandon what I actually think is true?
history.daily_action: In one conversation today, state your honest view plainly—without apology, without overexplaining, without checking their face for approval.
history.evening_question: Where did I perform agreement today, and what was I protecting—their comfort, or my own safety in their eyes?

history.daily_question: When I move through someone else's urgency today, can I notice what I actually want before I agree to want what they want?
history.carry_question: Whose urgency am I carrying right now, and is it actually mine?
history.surrender_question: Can I notice one place today where I am trying to earn something I neither need nor actually want?
history.daily_action: In one moment of decision or compliance today, pause and ask: Is this coming from me, or am I borrowing someone else's script? Then choose openly.
history.evening_question: What did I notice about the difference between moving with genuine agreement and moving to avoid conflict today?

history.echo_title: Song of the Open Road · section 13 · excerpt, stanza 8
history.daily_question: When I notice myself delighting in a good action, am I actually free—or am I still caught in the pleasure of self-approval?
history.carry_question: When I do something good today, can I notice what I'm actually feeling beneath the satisfaction?
history.surrender_question: What if the pleasure I take in my own goodness is not the problem, but a clue that something else wants to be seen?
history.daily_action: Do one ordinary good thing today without narrating it to yourself as good; notice what happens to the delight when you stop watching yourself.
history.evening_question: Did I catch myself performing approval today, and if so, what was the truth I was swallowing instead of speaking?

history.companion_title: Song of the Open Road · section 3
history.daily_question: When I notice myself watching my own actions today—censuring or approving—whose standard am I actually measuring against?
history.carry_question: When I encounter someone today, am I watching them as Epictetus watches himself, or receiving them as Whitman receives the ferry crowd?
history.surrender_question: Am I willing to notice that my judgment might be doing work I do not see—and let that curiosity interrupt the habit?
history.daily_action: Pick one moment today where you catch yourself evaluating—your action, your word, someone else's—and pause. Do not erase the judgment; notice where it came from and what it is protecting or proving.
history.evening_question: What did I notice about how I watched myself or others today, and was there a moment when I could have simply acted or received instead?
